content: A heave, also referred to as a lift, parasternal heave, parasternal lift, left ventricular impulse, or LV impulse, is a palpable upward movement of the chest wall that can be felt during the physical examination of the precordium. This sensation is typically detected when the examiner places the heel of their hand along the sternal border and feels for any abnormal displacement of the chest. For a more comprehensive understanding of the physical examination techniques related to the precordium, including the assessment of heaves, it is recommended to refer to the specific chapter on palpation of the precordium.
